title: RAW UNREVIEWED: compulsory equal-letter word liaison with an explicitly paid seam
summary: An invented dictionary-free hand convention joins neighboring lowercase source words only when the last letter of the first equals the first letter of the second. One written seam replaces the second copy and the source space; the reader restores both. Maximal eligible chains become one printed group. Full ordinary spelling, repeated words, capitalization and punctuation survive. No native word values, historical attestation or statistical fit is asserted.

design.mechanism: Within a source paragraph, join every adjacent pair of wholly lowercase a-z tokens whose boundary letters are identical. This is obligatory for all such pairs, never optional. At an eligible boundary omit the right token's first letter and write one explicit JOIN seam instead of the source space. Preserve every other character. All eligible seams in a maximal chain remain inside one printed group; every ineligible source space becomes an ordinary printed group space.
design.unit: One printed group is one maximal liaison chain, possibly a single unchanged source token. It is not invariably a source word or fixed-size source block. Output paragraph boundaries equal source paragraph boundaries. Physical line wraps carry no state and cannot cancel a required join.
design.contrast: No prior-word prefix copying, cache address, cyclic alphabet, word abbreviation list, source-character reordering or all-boundary shift. The rule redistributes source words among groups only at a source-local exact-letter condition and pays for each removed source boundary. It adds one general boundary convention to ordinary spelling, not a new lexical table.
design.prediction: After inverse decoding, every unjoined within-paragraph boundary between wholly lowercase a-z tokens must have unequal boundary letters. Any eligible equal-letter outer boundary contradicts the canonical writer. Every JOIN must follow a nonempty reconstructed lowercase token, starts the next token with exactly the previous last letter, and all tokens in that chain must remain lowercase a-z. No lexicon or semantic guess may repair a violation.
design.scope: Artificial source-preserving convention only. No existing Voynich form is assigned a source letter, word, meaning or a JOIN role by this proposal. The carrier is an explicitly artificial teaching key; native atomization, carrier binding and source-word interpretation remain assumptions requiring separate review.
design.source_contract: Nonempty tokens over lowercase a-z plus the listed56 auxiliary characters, separated by one space and with explicit paragraphs. Exact spelling, capitalization, punctuation, order and unresolved references are retained. Repeated whitespace and physical source lineation are outside the declared edition. An unlisted character fails rather than being normalized. A token containing any auxiliary character is ineligible for a join on either side.
design.encode: Inspect adjacent original source tokens from left to right. Write the first token in full. At an eligible boundary append JOIN and then all but the first character of the next token. Otherwise write a group space and the next token in full. Continue through the paragraph; write the paragraph break and restart. Eligibility always uses the original source tokens, including the one letter that may already have been shared. There is no lookahead beyond the next token's first character plus checking that its token is wholly lowercase.
design.decode: Parse the fixed character carrier and JOIN units. Start each printed group with an empty current source token. A literal character appends that character. At JOIN require the current token nonempty and entirely lowercase a-z; save its last letter c, finish that source token, and start the next token with c. At printed group end finish the current nonempty token. Reject a later auxiliary character anywhere in a joined chain. Finally check all outer group boundaries against the obligatory join condition. Reading can stream; canonical validation of a token's lowercase eligibility waits until that token is complete.
design.edge_cases: A JOIN may end a group when the right source token has one letter. Consecutive JOINs are legal and each creates a distinct one-letter source token. JOIN cannot start a group. For invented abstract source characters, ab|b|bc becomes ab JOIN JOIN c and decodes to all three exact words. ab|ba becomes ab JOIN a; abba alone remains abba, so its different source boundary is retained. These are artificial string examples, not native readings.

teaching_carrier.lowercase: Source a-s use the nineteen ordinary signs in order. Source t-z use q followed by the first seven ordinary signs. These are stipulated teaching assignments, not inferred native sound values.
teaching_carrier.auxiliary: For zero-based auxiliary index j, write cfh then ordinary[floor(j/19)] then ordinary[j mod19]. Reject codes j>=56. All nineteen ordinary signs are possible selectors; this is a complete public radix19 indexing rule, not an additional word table.
teaching_carrier.join: cph is the single JOIN marker. It never occurs inside a literal character code. The19 ordinary signs, q, cfh and cph are the entire22 working inventory. A character code is one ordinary sign, q+one selector, or cfh+two selectors; the arities and disjoint prefixes make them uniquely parseable.
teaching_carrier.rendering_limit: Multi-letter EVA names label single stipulated drawing units. Their unique segmentation in native material is not established here. No choice of palette or native key has been optimized; the teaching key is not selected as a Voynich realization. The full19-selector auxiliary convention was fixed while drafting this new mechanism, after reading the known rare-form report; no pre-exposure claim is made.

design.learning_and_memory_cost: 26 lowercase correspondences,56 ordered auxiliary-character correspondences with a radix19 lookup, one JOIN convention and ordinary source-language literacy. There is no stored word dictionary. The writer needs the current boundary letter and access to two adjacent source tokens; the reader retains one last source character and a lowercase-eligibility flag, plus the current word/output buffer of unbounded word length. No hidden counter or recipe history is used. JOIN generally replaces one letter code plus the source space, so no general ink-saving claim follows, especially when a letter already has one glyph.

known_observation_obligations.repetition: Equal neighboring written groups are not universally banned and do not have one compulsory initial. A source word whose first and last letters differ may repeat as separate groups; one whose ends agree must instead join. This is a specific conditional restriction, not an escape clause. The documented daiin/chedy/ol and other duplicate witnesses remain obligations for any independently selected carrier. An arbitrary repeated glyph substring is not automatically one whole letter code.
known_observation_obligations.terminals: Ordinary one-token groups and joined groups can end in many ordinary signs, including y/r/l in the teaching alphabet, or JOIN after a one-letter token. The940two-final invariant is not imposed.
known_observation_obligations.extremes: Unchanged single source words can be short, rare or arbitrarily long. Joined chains can also be long. This does not explain why cheoltchedaiin is written as one group, identify cheol|tchedaiin as its source boundary, or make every long group a contraction. The observed long connected form and its alternate formal parses remain independent obligations. The report's cfham/kydainy/ckholsy forms receive no meanings from the teaching key.
known_observation_obligations.f45r: The complete retained f45r.10 line must be kept in any later binding check. No cell-balance, fixed group length, pure-END reset or universal terminal constraint is imposed. No native inverse or outcome check was performed here, and no claim that the whole line passes follows merely from the absence of those old invariants.

design.smallest_useful_falsifier: Before any corpus encoding, a fixed carrier plus an already owned definite outer seam can refute the canonical rule if its two decoded tokens are wholly lowercase and have equal boundary letters. A structural proof would need complete code-unit alignment, not merely matching edge glyphs. Conversely, displaying a legal long synthetic chain proves only reversibility, not usefulness or native fit. Any later source necessary-frequency test would use one frozen source edition and this one exact grouping rule; no sweep of join conditions is proposed.

predecessors.difference: The failed universal one-character boundary displacement preserves a different group count and moves every inner boundary. This conditional coalescence removes only matching-letter boundaries and carries each removed boundary explicitly; its old failure remains.
Those group by exact function-word membership or length. No such list, threshold, or adjustment is used. Exact936was not itself executed by1176/77; its literal final-y failure remains scoped.
No maximal prior-word prefix, recency buffer, two-terminal framing or shrinking column state; all their known fixed contradictions remain.

883closes fixed overlapping latent blocks at every written adjacency. Here literal characters retain independent codes; sharing occurs only at an overt paid source-word seam. No homogeneous overlapping-block hypothesis is revived.

Its zero exact cross-folio resegmentation capacity is retained. A JOIN both removes one duplicate source character and adds an explicit operator, so this rule does not predict unchanged raw-string conservation with merely relocated spaces.
The lexical route-check hit concerns a particular semantic same/cross-material joining table, not source-letter liaison; its188failed literal branches are unrelated and unchanged.
Reusable directed parts and transparent macro confluence are prior knowledge. This proposal neither rediscovers them nor claims to account for native whole-form residuals.
